summary: Delegated idempotency scope normalization mismatch via multi-tenant proxy causing partial tool side-effects
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when using a delegated service account pattern (AcmeAI proxies requests through their tenancy router), long-running function/tool calls occasionally complete but downstream side-effects (webhook calls, database writes) are executed twice or partially applied. The duplicate/partial side-effects appear only when the request path traverses AcmeAI's multi-tenant reverse proxy which injects a Delegated-Id header and rewrites some incoming headers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sets up a delegated-service flow: client -> AcmeAI tenancy-proxy -> Redwood API (prod/us-east) using a delegated service key.
2) Client issues a streaming function-call that triggers an external webhook (tool) with idempotency metadata set at the request scope (X-Idempotency-Key).
3) Proxy rewrites headers (normalization step) and attaches Delegated-Id and X-Account-Tenant headers. Proxy also base64-url encodes a portion of the id when forwarding to Redwood.

4) Intermittently, SDK (python/node) retries the call after transient network hiccup; Redwood serving-runtime accepts and runs the tool but webhook receives either duplicated POSTs or a single POST with duplicate side-effect application (e.g., two partial DB upserts).
5) Observe server logs and webhook endpoint traces for duplicate deliveries correlated with a modified idempotency key seen at Redwood's ingress.
Expected: A single external side-effect per idempotent request regardless of proxy header rewrites or delegated key flows.
logs: 2026-03-09T15:23:11Z redwood-api-gateway INFO incoming request key=acct:acme:1234 x-idempotency-key=client-8f3a (received) delegated-id=proxy-B64-Q2FjZQ==
Proxy logs (AcmeAI) show header-rewrite event at 15:23:10Z: normalized idempotency key truncated to 16 chars and suffix added: client-8f3a__proxy-B64
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header normalization at customer proxy mutates idempotency key namespace so Redwood treats retried attempt as a distinct idempotency scope.

Observed that some proxies truncate long Id keys and append a tenant suffix; this leads to two distinct keys arriving at the API depending on where truncation occurred in the call path (client vs proxy).

SDK behavior: python SDK will reattach the original X-Idempotency-Key when retrying, but if the proxy has already rewritten the header on first request, subsequent attempts may traverse a different internal path (edge cache vs direct) and be rewritten differently, producing two unique keys at the gateway.
Serving-runtime dedup semantics are per-normalized-key + model-route. If the normalization differs mid-flight, dedup cannot correlate the two attempts.
We confirmed one reproduction with curl via AcmeAI proxy that reproduces duplicate webhook deliveries when proxy truncation limit < 24 bytes and appends tenant suffix.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Reproduced with AcmeAI proxy settings. Captured 2 request IDs (rwd-9091, rwd-9092) where payload identical but X-Idempotency-Key differed. Sent example logs to SRE.

2026-03-10 11:45 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Confirmed behavior. Gateway currently normalizes id keys by JSON canonicalization but does not canonicalize delegated-id suffixes added by proxies. Creating short-term filter to strip known proxy suffix pattern before idempotency normalization in ingress.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Customer (AcmeAI): We cannot remove tenant suffix addition due to our routing requirements. Looking for guidance on preserving single-delivery semantics without changing our platform.

2026-03-11 08:15 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Proposed workaround: recommend clients set an explicit Idempotency-Scope header carrying an immutable UUID generated at client origin; SDKs can set this header for users. Also planning a gateway ingress change: detect and collapse tenant-suffix patterns into a single canonical key for delegated flows. PR pending review.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Product (Riley Chen): Note: must validate that canonicalization does not collide across true distinct requests in multi-tenant environments. Add tests for cross-tenant collisions and audit logs for normalization events.
resolution: Workaround provided: instruct AcmeAI to configure SDK to send Idempotency-Scope header (client-generated UUID) and avoid relying on proxy-modified X-Idempotency-Key. Short-term ingress patch added to gateway to strip recognized proxy-suffix patterns for delegated flows; patch deployed to prod/us-east behind a feature flag. Follow-ups: write automated tests to ensure canonicalization safety, add telemetry to detect future normalization mismatches, coordinate with customer to evaluate removing tenant suffixing or using a fixed client-side idempotency header. Pending code PR #2893 for permanent ingress normalization and SDK convenience helpers.
next_steps: 1) Merge and roll out PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2893 which adds SDK helper to set Idempotency-Scope header in python/ts SDKs.
2) Complete gateway canonicalization review and add robust dedup tests across tenant-suffix edge cases (owner: Marcus).
3) Schedule 30-minute sync with AcmeAI engineering to discuss proxy header behavior and long-term mitigation (owner: CS lead).
4) Add an alert to console when incoming request idempotency keys vary across retry attempts for the same client request ID (observability owner).
